doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: People with class; Hutcherson, Tyner and Hancock as improvisers
summary: They discuss musicians whose class rubs off, and Marshall names Hutcherson, McCoy Tyner and Herbie Hancock as great improvisers.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Some of those — there’s people that you just — we were talking with Earl Watkins — that have a certain amount of class to them, it rubs off on you.
You know like I always think of Milt Hinton and guys like that.
Yeah I never got a chance to meet Milt Hinton.
Yeah. But those are the kind of people that you feel better after you hang out with them.

I know it. I know it. Oh boy. Bobby Hutcherson is another one. Bobby and McCoy Tyner — they seem to be two of the greatest improvisers that I can— You know if I think of pure improvising? And I’d have to add Herbie Hancock into that too. That they can just take, you know just bend harmony or whatever they do, everything is so pliable in their hands.
